findings.text: Upheld as advisory. `parseYaml` is copied word for word from tests/unit/deploy-files.test.ts:10. Duplicated test boilerplate falls under question 2, which the rubric treats as advisory.

Upheld as advisory. The fake checksums file (REQUIRED_ASSETS without checksums.txt, mapped to repeat(64) digests) is also built by the new `checksums()` helper in tests/integration/release-commands.test.ts. This is test fixture logic written twice (question 2).

Upheld as advisory. `gitStub`'s option `quote?: "clone"` can take only one value, so it is a boolean written as a literal type. Its name also does not say that it makes the clone fail (questions 3 and 5). Naming in a test helper does not make the code wrong.

Upheld as advisory. The rewritten security row drops the old row's claim that Actions masks the raw secret only, and does not say that this claim was corrected (question 11). The row is closed, and ADR 0029 now gives the source (ValueEncoders.cs), so the record is not left wrong.

Upheld as advisory. AC-22's ADR test checks only for the bare token "`::add-mask::`". It does not check that the ADR says the runner masks a secret's base64 itself, or why no such line is printed. The test still fails when the change is reverted, so this is partial coverage under question 1, not a missing test.

Upheld as advisory. The findings-row test checks "`PUSH_REMOTE`" and "`timeout-minutes`" but not "`PUSH_ORIGIN`". It checks the open time-limit item only by the loose phrase "time limit". This is partial coverage under question 1. The test fails on revert.

Upheld as advisory. `redact` covers only the base64 header form, not the raw MARKETPLACE_TOKEN. No path in the diff prints the raw token: git is never handed it, and the runner masks it as a registered secret. ADR 0029 states the exact-match limit, so this is hardening only.

Lowered to advisory as debt outside the change. `gitEnv(token, process.env)` passes the inherited environment to the token's git calls, and only the inherited GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n is overwritten. A home .gitconfig, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL or system configuration can still steer that git. The diff does not add this, and docs/real-use/findings.md records it as deferred.
Lowered to advisory as debt outside the change. The git calls that carry no header still inherit MARKETPLACE_TOKEN. This is recorded as deferred in docs/real-use/findings.md.
Lowered to advisory as debt outside the change. The file is not in the diff. The git calls of push.ts have no time limit of their own beyond the job's. This is recorded as deferred.

Upheld as advisory. The cut-job paragraph rests on two values nobody has measured: that the dispatch finishes within 5 minutes, and that a late-accepted run appears within a minute. The harm is bounded, because a second run writes nothing the first already wrote. A cut is visible as a red release.yml. spec.md states the rollback as a revert on main. No rollback or dependency is missing from the spec or plan, so there is no defect.

Lowered to advisory as debt outside the change. The file is not in the diff. The headerless git calls inherit MARKETPLACE_TOKEN and the global and system git configuration, and they have no time limit of their own. The item records all three as deferred in docs/real-use/findings.md, and the diff does not widen them.

Dropped as a finding and noted as advisory. Line 73 is not a line of the diff (the hunk ends at line 60), and the note states a known unknown that the item itself records as deferred: whether the runner masks a secret's base64 in the step summary. It names no rubric failure in the change.

Upheld as advisory. Nobody has measured whether `timeout-minutes: 5` on the dispatch-only job is enough, so a slow API day may show a false red. The rollback is stated, and the runbook gives the recovery steps (docs/runbooks/release.md, the new paragraph). This is the reviewer's own advisory under Q4.

Upheld as advisory. `redact` matches only the exact base64 of the credential, not the raw token. git is never handed the raw value, and ADR 0029 states the limit (Q2). This is the same point as security F-1.

Lowered to advisory as debt outside the change. release.yml still references its actions by moving tag, and its checkouts keep credentials under a workflow-level contents: write. The diff does not touch these lines, and docs/real-use/findings.md already records them as deferred.

Lowered to advisory as debt outside the change. The calls without the header inherit MARKETPLACE_TOKEN, the token's git is not isolated from global and system configuration, and the git calls have no time limit of their own. The item names all three as deferred.
